reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and isDailyWeekendSkip and threads holidays through them, though schedule-template.ts builds its own closure instead of calling the new getWeekendAdjustedDate helper.

duplication.why: Removes the two repeated adjust ternaries in schedule-template and the filter/map pairs in app.ts, but the schedule-template closure re-states the skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(...) : date logic that getWeekendAdjustedDate now encapsulates, and getNextDate keeps its own variant.

placement.why: The day-off predicate and shifting logic live in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing weekend helpers, the type in RecurConfig, and the rule-utils mapping carries the field into rschedule data.

scope.why: All edits serve the holidays feature plus tests; the small refactors are in the touched code paths.

maintainability.why: One isWeekendOrHoliday predicate drives both skip and shift, which is easy to own; the ad hoc window padding (2 x holidays length) and the three slightly different adjust wrappers are minor warts.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All sites route through getDateWithSkippedWeekend/isWeekendOrHoliday; schedule-template uses a local closure rather than getWeekendAdjustedDate but still calls the shared function.

disguised_duplication.where: schedule-template.ts getAdjustedDate closure re-implements getWeekendAdjustedDate (skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(date, mode, holidays) : date) with string conversion around it.

one_place.where: isWeekendOrHoliday in shared/schedules.ts is used by getDateWithSkippedWeekend, getNextDate's daily skip and app.ts applyWeekendHandling, so the holiday-as-weekend rule is defined once.
